Subject: Re: [UAI] causal direction of BN?

Li Guoliang wrote:
> Hi,
> 
> You can find some references or algorithms in the following three books.
> 
> 1. Causation, prediction, and search
> Peter Spirtes, Clark Glymour, and Richard Scheines ; with additional
> material by David Heckerman ... [et al.] 
> Cambridge, Mass. : MIT Press, c2000. 
> Edition 2nd ed.
> 
> 2. Computation, causation, and discovery
> edited by Clark Glymour and Gregory F. Cooper. 
> Menlo Park, Calif. : AAAI Press ; Cambridge, Mass. : MIT Press, c1999 
> 
> 3. Causality : models, reasoning, and inference
> Judea Pearl. 
> Cambridge, U.K. ; New York : Cambridge University Press, 2000

In addition, a freely available implementation (an ASP solution) can be 
found at http://b-course.hiit.fi (also with some supporting material).

Go all the way through the "D-trail" (use the example data sets if you 
do not have data of your own), and then choose either "Naive causal 
model" or "Not-so-naive causal model". The first option uses models with 
no latent variables, while the second considers also models with latent 
variables that are parents of exactly two observed variables.

All the best,

--Petri
